english_verification.review_scope: Representative current-Mod opening history and English flavour names; related offline English Wiki passage for drakons and Gor Vazumbrog; no exhaustive mission-tree audit. Native English idea names/descriptions were compared by localisation key with the current Mod. Wide line ranges locate separately read passages, not exhaustive coverage. No formal validator, build, browser or gameplay test was run. The primary reread the hold Fall passage (including 894), the Shadowdreamer identity stub and English flavour lines 1–60.
unresolved: No dedicated offline English Wiki country page for Skewered Drake was returned; the Wiki evidence supports drakon identity and origin context only, not the full H73 history or current mechanisms.
The practical execution details of some Drakonshan authority labour interactions remain unverified in-game.

rationale.campaign_length: The 43 direct missions are divided between tribal and Drakonshan stages, with objectives extending into the mid and late game.
rationale.colonization: Underground exploration and colonisation are prominent early; conquest and subject management dominate later.
rationale.complexity: You must manage underground expansion, drakon growth, staged missions, authority and subjects at the same time.
rationale.dark_story: Active conquest, forced submission and institutionalised resource extraction run through the imperial stage.
rationale.difficulty: Cavalry is powerful, but subject and cross-region mission thresholds make long-term planning difficult.
rationale.diplomacy: A large subject network, authority and liberty desire are central management concerns.
rationale.early_pressure: The opening contests underground routes and resources while waiting for territorial and mission thresholds.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: The core is drakon taming and cavalry, with no evidence of a magic or artificery system of comparable weight.
rationale.narrative_density: A ruined tribe, drakon symbiosis, underground unification and an overlord empire create a continuous sequence of turns.
rationale.tall_play: Dens, mining and development of the core area matter, but the end state requires a large subject network and cross-region territory.
rationale.trade_economy: Loot, metal and subject resources fund war; trade is not the exclusive core loop.
rationale.warfare: Mythical drakon cavalry, underground hold warfare and surface conquest are the campaign's main axes.

identity.appearance: A black-orc starting country in the middle Serpentspine in 1444; it is renamed Drakonshan in the middle of the campaign and switches to the later missions while retaining H73.

successors.relationship: A mission event renames the country, grants the Drakonshan Dominion government and opens the second-stage missions under the same Tag.
An optional generic formation detour; after changing Tag, H73-exclusive missions no longer meet their display condition.

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas and ambition only; optional idea groups and racial/government bonuses are excluded. Conditional alternatives are separate, not stacked. Accepting new ideas on formation depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

description.text: Born from the howling pit within Gor Vazumbrog, the scar left behind by the Hunter of the Deep's awakening, come the great Drakons upon which we ride. These beasts who were the apex predator of the middle Serpentspine, pending our arrival, are vicious creatures, naturally built for battle. Their reddish-black scales are as durable as diamonds, their bodies long and slender to weave between stalagmites with ease. Their pitch-black talons are capable of rending muscle and bone alike, doubling as tools with which to latch onto and run along the walls of the tunnels. The only way to make them more dangerous was to put our orcs upon them. Saddled upon these drakes we put our finest warriors to ride into battle causing devastating damage. As the drake tears through lines the orc finishes those left in its carnage, directing it from above to its next target.

description.text: Of the many terrible sights one might encounter among the dark annals of the Serpentspine, few would dispute that a Drakon rider is among the most frightening. Covered in bioluminescent algae, menacing images of death and terror are sprawled across these mounts. In a flurry of colors and pictures, they dash by in the tunnels. Should you manage to avoid this blur of light, it was most likely at the whim of the orc above so that he may get the kill personally.

description.text: Emulating the Drakons they ride, the Skewered Drake warriors have managed to fashion iron rakes that they can attach to their hands and latch onto walls with. Much like a Drakon can scale cliffs, now they can too. Climbing over walls, the Skewered Drake warriors are able to bypass defenses otherwise impenetrable.

description.text: To cook a drake, one often skewers it and roasts its chunks over a fire, proving tremendously difficult due to their size and the strength of their muscles. To overcome this, Skewered Drake have become masters at sharpening and crafting massive skewers to cook them and other beasts they come across. In fact, many orcs of the clan now carry these skewers around with them at all times when out traversing the Serpentspine; in numbers they are able to make camp with them by repurposing these skewers as palisades wherever they go.

description.text: The toughness of a drake's scales can not be understated; it is no wonder then that they would make such excellent tools. A drake's diamond-hard scales can be fashioned into a multitude of things, such as armor, but most importantly into pickaxes, hammers, and shovels. These tools are capable of mining tough ores and rocks, and should these tools ever chip or break there will always be more scales in short time.

description.text: A regular sporting event held by the chieftains of the Skewered Drake, these so called 'Fight Nights' are where they pit two drakes up against each other in a battle to the death. To add to the fervor of the event, orcs are allowed to bet on the winner in the hopes of making quick coin. In the end, no matter who wins the fight or bets, the chieftain gets a cut of the pool and the clan gets that much richer from it.

description.text: Gorrath may be known as the Wrathful but he was not merely a brute; he was also tremendously clever, utilizing the existing layout of the ruined hold to administrate efficiently and effectively. It is due to this that the Skewered Drake clan has managed to maintain stability for hundreds of years with relative ease whereas many of their brethren in the Serpentspine have failed.

description.text:
Bloodshed is all our people has ever known. Best our enemies and take everything they have, once merely to survive, but no longer now that the mountain-home and its wealth are orcishkind’s dominion. We will take from the strong, not because we need to, but because we are stronger.

Raids outside the Serpentspine will be overseen by the Algakar Code, which ensures fair treatment of prisoners until they are ransomed, forbids attacks on towns that haven’t finished rebuilding, and states that those who accept to pay tribute shall be left alone. The rules ensure the surfacers know what to expect of us, so that they give up as much riches as possible. But more importantly, they allow the weak to rebuild and grow richer.
And once they gather enough wealth, we will take everything from them too, because we are stronger.

description.text:
In the darkness of the Dwarovar, the trader and explorer needs light, but the raider prowls in the dark. Black orcs have invented many fighting techniques adapted to the darkness along the centuries, and the unification of orcishkind has refined them into a martial art of its own that foregoes reliance on sight entirely.

The greatest blademasters of that art undergo a ceremony in which they gouge out their own eyes to rely solely on Dookan’s sight instead of their own, and emerge Unchained. Even other orcs fear such masters; they whisper of seemingly impossible counters to attacks that were not even started, of a terrifying implacable fighting pace and believe them undefeatable in combat.

description.text: Dookan teaches that thinking of war without keeping peace in mind is madness, and that thinking of peace without keeping war in mind is foolishness. There is a time for all things, and what truly keeps us together isn’t the glory we share in battle. It’s the family we come back to, and the smile of a son or daughter welcoming us home. One day, they too shall know war, but as Dookan teaches, there is a time for all things, and nothing is more sacred in Tarakar than a child’s innocence.

description.text:
Everything. Everything one desires can be acquired in an Ozarm’chadash, ensuring he has the strength to claim it. Such is the informal rule of those duels the participants implicitly agree on.

Still, the nature of such a challenge makes people wary of issuing them unless they have nothing left to lose, and they don’t hone our people’s skills as much as they could. We will replace those duels of honor to settle disputes by ritualized gladiatorial combats to keep us strong. Anyone who wishes to acquire greater status, wealth, or fame can enter the arena to claim it, and the last one standing -even should it be a mean enough dwarf or the odd honorable goblin- will have earned it by right of strength, the only one that matters. Such is the way we orcs live by, and the only true way.

description.text:
“-That map of yours was right, Mushû. Tons of good salvage in there. The bearded really don’t make stuff as they used to.
-I think of that often, answered Mushû the Philosopher, because they called him that for a reason. They fell apart because of all those giant halls they dug and giant statues they made to fill them.
-You ain’t making any sense.
-They were full of themselves. Wanted to be remembered, but only built their own tomb instead. We’ll make something out of it, and it’s going to be used by our people and not sitting there looking fancy.
-Uh, never thought of it like that. Guess that’s why they call you the Philosopher.
-Just remember, we’re giving new life to every piece we take back. We’re not just scavengers. We’re builders of the future.
-Yeah, well, the future can wait a bit. These pieces are heavy.”

As they got to work, Gralk couldn't help but wonder if there was some truth to Mushû's words. Maybe they were more than just scavengers. Maybe, just maybe, they were part of something bigger.

description.text:
To become Tarakar’s ruler, one must destroy all obstacles on their way. To rule Tarakar is to rule unchallenged. Orcs may once have followed local chiefs, but there is now only one being strong enough to be worth following under the mountains.

Our realm itself shall acknowledge that truth, and from bickering tribes something new, something stronger will be forged. Out of the blood spilt in unseen caverns and the fire of the Serpentspine’s forges, a true nation of orcs will emerge.

description.text:
We orcs hold within us the spark legated by Dookan himself, his divinity our own. A gift, but also a duty to free him from the unjust imprisonment inflicted upon him by the treacherous other gods as he wanted to find a new home for himself and us.

However, numerous variations of the story can be found all across the Serpentspine. We will work on compiling them and creating a unified version of the true teachings of Dookan, and orcish scholars will become Tarakar’s warriors in the greatest of all conflicts! Freeing a god is not a task that can be achieved by mortal steel; Dookan’s cage shall be broken by making the followers of the traitor gods turn away from them to weaken their power. Only then shall their treachery be undone!

player_overview.avoid_if: Avoid this route if you dislike early underground waiting, specified subject and territorial thresholds, or managing authority and subject liberty desire together.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Colonise underground and seize holds first, funding drakon cavalry with loot; develop dens and mines in the middle game, reform into the Drakonshan Dominion, then manage many subjects while conquering across regions.
player_overview.overview: You begin as a black-orc tribe in the middle Serpentspine, contesting dwarven holds and underground roads with drakon companions. After the first conquests the country becomes Drakonshan, shifting toward authority, subjects, mining and drakon armies before expanding into Bulwar and farther afield.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy unusual cavalry, black orcs, underground exploration, long-term expansion and running a subject empire.
signature_features: Mythical cavalry fighting alongside drakons, with a growing ruler's mount, makes cavalry the campaign's protagonist.
Two mission stages turn a raiding tribe into a subject empire while retaining the original Tag.
Dedicated authority can levy labour, extract subject resources and hold tournaments, while coercive demands increase governing costs.
player_overview.tagline: Tame drakons, dominate the underground, and build a Drakonshan empire through cavalry and subjects.

reasons: Drakon companions and mythical cavalry create a genuinely distinctive military protagonist.
The tribal-to-Drakonshan renaming creates a clear story transition into a subject empire.
Authority, subject resources and liberty desire create actionable governing trade-offs.
warnings: Early underground expansion and mission unlocks may require waiting.
The latter half carries a high burden of subject, territory and authority management.
Forming M04 Tarakar means H73-exclusive missions no longer meet their Tag condition.

values.rationale: Forced submission, subject labour and development extraction are real forms of coercion, but less severe than slavery, treating people as resources or extermination. Some labour interactions still need in-game confirmation, so the old model should not push the country into the lowest values tier.
